beats.text: With Rama gone, Ayodhya lost its light. No fires were lit, no songs were sung, and the markets were empty.
When Sumantra returned with the empty chariot, the king fainted.
Dasharatha cried Rama's name day and night. Then he remembered a curse from long ago.
As a young prince, he had shot an arrow at a sound in the dark, thinking it was an elephant drinking.
It was a young hermit filling a pot of water for his blind parents. Later tellings call him Shravan Kumar.
The grieving parents cursed him: 'You too will die of grief, separated from your son.'
Now the curse had come true. On the sixth night, at midnight, he whispered, 'Rama, Rama,' and was gone.
At dawn, the queens found him still. The whole palace broke into cries.
